blocks.text: Setting up Gmail for customer support specialists on mac

Since Google does not provide a native Gmail application for macOS, you must rely on your web browser. This is actually a benefit because you can use browser-specific features to stay organized. Start by creating a dedicated web app. In Safari, go to File > Add to Dock. In Chrome, go to the three-dot menu > Save and Share > Install page as app. This puts a Gmail icon directly in your Dock, making it feel like a standalone application.

Once you have your icon, you need to enable keyboard shortcuts. They are off by default. Click the Settings gear icon in the top right, then click See all settings. Under the General tab, scroll down to the Keyboard shortcuts section. Select Keyboard shortcuts on. Click Save Changes at the bottom of the page. Now you can press the ? key at any time to see a full list of available commands.

Customer support agents often handle 30 to 50 tickets every day. You cannot afford to click through menus for every action. Use the core shortcuts to save time. Press c to compose a new message, r to reply, and a to reply all. When you finish a ticket, press e to archive it. This keeps your inbox clean and ensures you only see active requests. If a thread needs attention later, press b to snooze it until a specific time.

Labels are your best friend for organizing incoming requests. Create specific labels for different issue types, such as Billing, Technical Support, or Feedback. You can automate this process by creating filters. Go to Settings > Filters and Blocked Addresses > Create a new filter. You can set rules based on the sender or keywords in the subject line. This ensures that every email lands in the right place automatically.

If you are stuck on a specific Gmail feature, hold Option + Command to ask Lazur where it is. Lazur will circle the button or menu on your screen.

blocks.title: Get guided help

blocks.text: You can also use Lazur to draft responses. Hold the fn key to dictate your reply. Lazur handles the formatting, so you can focus on the tone of your message. This is helpful when you need to write a long explanation for a technical issue. It saves you from repetitive typing and helps you maintain a consistent voice across all your customer interactions.
Common Gmail mistakes for support agents

items: Forgetting to check the CC or BCC fields before hitting send on a sensitive ticket.
Relying on manual replies instead of using canned responses or templates.
Leaving the inbox cluttered with old threads that are already resolved.
Failing to use search operators to find specific attachments or older customer history.
Ignoring the display density settings, which can make it harder to scan your queue quickly.

blocks.text: Many agents struggle with finding information quickly. Learn to use search operators. For example, use has:attachment to find emails with files. You can also search by date using older_than:30d. These small skills add up over the course of a week. They help you keep your handle time closer to the 8 minute mark rather than the 25 minute mark for complex tickets.

If you work in a team, you might need to give someone else access to your mailbox. You can do this by going to Settings > Accounts and Import > Grant access to your account. This is useful for shared support inboxes. Just be careful with who you add to ensure data security. Always review your account permissions periodically to ensure only the right people have access.

Sometimes you need to send an email later. Maybe you are working on a ticket at 6 PM but want the customer to receive it during business hours. Use the schedule send feature. Instead of clicking the big Send button, click the small arrow next to it. Select Schedule send. Choose a date and time that works best for your customer. This simple step can improve your response quality by ensuring emails arrive when they are most likely to be read.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native desktop app for Gmail on macOS. You should use a web browser like Chrome or Safari and create a web app shortcut to get a similar experience.

faq.question: How do I turn on keyboard shortcuts in Gmail?
faq.answer: Go to Settings > See all settings > General. Scroll down to Keyboard shortcuts and select Keyboard shortcuts on. Don't forget to click Save Changes.

faq.question: What is the daily sending limit for Gmail?
faq.answer: Personal accounts can send to up to 500 recipients per day. Google Workspace accounts have a higher limit of up to 2,000 recipients per day.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me in Gmail?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It can point at buttons on your screen, guide you through steps, or dictate text, but you remain in control of your mouse and keyboard.
